thought: the Chancellor lets anyone in; Osman's standing gripe
line: The Chancellor would trust a camel if it bowed nicely.

thought: he did his wandering young, and is content to watch now
line: I did my wandering young. Now I stand still and the world walks past.

thought: his creed: quiet work, no needless blood
line: Quiet work is good work. Loud work gets people buried.

thought: a stranger lingered looking at the palace; he files the face
line: Another stranger staring at the palace. I shall remember that face.

thought: the Menaphites would know him on sight; he is quietly proud of it
line: Every Menaphite knows my face. I take that as a compliment.

thought: the desert has no single ruler, which is his trade
line: The desert has many masters and no king. That keeps me busy.

thought: why he stands outside the palace all day, wryly
line: Nobody stands outside a palace all day for the view.

thought: peace with old rivals is only peace for now; he trusts it as far as he can see
line: Peace with the Menaphites, for now. I count it daily, like coins.

thought: the stranger passed without a sound; that matters more to him than steel
line: You walk quietly. That is worth more than a sword.

thought: they kept their mouth shut as they passed
line: Not a word out of you as you passed. I approve.

thought: he sizes them up as someone who might keep a secret
line: Perhaps you could keep a secret. We shall see.

thought: they didn't gawp at the palace, unlike most
line: Hm. You did not stare at the palace. Most do.

thought: he files people away; this one goes in a decent drawer
line: I have filed you under 'possibly useful'. Do not make me refile you.

thought: they asked him nothing, which is the right number of questions
line: Fewer questions than most. I like that in a stranger.

thought: measures them by his own young adventuring days
line: You remind me of myself, long ago. Before I had the sense to stay put.

thought: to a guard nearby: that one keeps their eyes down, as a spy would
line: That one keeps their eyes to themselves. Sensible.

thought: the same adventurer again; he'd hoped they'd moved on
line: You again. I had hoped the desert would keep you.

thought: adventurers are noisy; he heard this one long before he saw them
line: I heard you three streets away. Adventurers walk like camels.

thought: they're trying to be inconspicuous, and failing
line: If you are trying to look inconspicuous, do keep trying.

thought: the idea of this one as a spy amuses him
line: A spy? You? I would sooner hire the camel.

thought: they're gawping at the palace too long
line: Stare at the palace any longer and I shall charge you rent.

thought: aside to someone: this one would blab for a snack
line: That one would sell the Emir's secrets for a kebab. Watch them.

thought: adventurers claim to keep secrets; he has heard that before
line: They say adventurers can keep a secret. They say a great many things.

thought: they talk too loudly near the spymaster's ears
line: Talk less. This city's walls have ears, and most of them are mine.

thought: the prince is taken; Hassan wants a hero, Osman wants a plan
line: The prince is gone, and the Chancellor wants a hero. I want a plan.

thought: heroics endanger hostages; he prefers quiet
line: Heroes make noise. Noise gets princes killed.

thought: Hassan sends him every would-be rescuer and he must sort them
line: Hassan sends me every stranger with a sword. I sift them.

thought: he knows more than he lets on, and that's the job
line: I know more of the prince than I say. That is rather the point.

thought: muttering his rule to himself
line: Quietly. It must be done quietly, or not at all.

thought: someone let the heir be taken, and it wasn't the spymaster
line: The Emir's heir taken. Someone was careless, and it was not me.

thought: Hassan frets; fretting achieves nothing
line: Fretting has never yet brought a prince home. Tell the Chancellor.

thought: he has eyes on the matter, not blades
line: Eyes, not swords. That is how one finds a missing prince.

thought: aside: steady and quiet, the sort the palace needs right now
line: Steady eyes, quiet feet. The palace could do worse, these days.

thought: they didn't ask what he does here; good start
line: You did not ask what I do here. Already you are ahead of most.

thought: sizing them up as a possible answer to the palace's trouble
line: Hm. You might be what the palace needs. Might.

thought: not hero material, which to him is praise
line: Not a hero, I think. Something more useful than that.

thought: discretion is at a premium while the prince is gone
line: You keep your counsel. In these times, that is worth a great deal.

thought: a stranger who doesn't gossip; rarer than rain here
line: A stranger who does not gossip. Rarer than rain, in this city.

thought: they carry themselves like someone who has done hard things quietly
line: You carry yourself like someone who has done hard things quietly.

thought: he has watched them pass before and they never looked back
line: I have watched you pass before. You never once looked back. Good.

thought: the prince is missing and here comes a sightseer
line: The prince needs finding, and here comes a tourist.

thought: Hassan would hire this one, which is exactly the problem
line: You? Hassan would hire you. That is precisely the trouble.

thought: they're loud; the prince's takers could hear them
line: Shout any louder and whoever took the prince will hear you.

thought: he took their measure on approach, and it was short
line: I took your measure as you came. A short measure, I am afraid.

thought: the palace wants a hero and may have to make do
line: The palace wants a hero. It may have to settle for you.

thought: aside: as subtle as a camel in a tent
line: Subtle as a camel in a tent, that one.

thought: word has spread that Hassan will hire anyone, and here they are
line: Word is the Chancellor will hire anyone. I see the word has spread.

thought: every adventurer imagines they're a spy
line: Every stranger thinks they would make a spy. You think so too.

thought: Leela reports the jail is quiet; he likes quiet
line: Leela reports the jail is quiet. Quiet suits me.

thought: the key plan is simple, in his view
line: A clay imprint and a bronze bar. Keys are simple things, really.

thought: 'Lady' Keli is self-styled; he is not impressed
line: Keli calls herself a lady. I have met camels with better manners.

thought: pride in his daughter's watch on the jail
line: My daughter watches that jail better than any guard I could hire.

thought: the disguise plan is absurd and he knows it
line: Dressing the prince as Keli is absurd. That is why it will work.

thought: an old jail east of Draynor, of all places
line: East of Draynor, of all places. Bandits have no taste in jails.

thought: as little blood as possible; that's professionalism
line: As little blood as possible. That is how a professional does it.

thought: Hassan has already got the reward ready, too soon
line: The Chancellor has his reward counted already. Counting chickens.

thought: they've been discreet about the plan so far
line: So far you have been discreet. Keep it so.

thought: Leela's report on them is grudgingly good
line: Leela says you have not yet made a nuisance of yourself. High praise.

thought: they may actually bring the prince back, against his odds
line: You may yet bring the prince home. I would not have bet on it.

thought: they heard the whole plan out without interrupting
line: You heard the whole plan without interrupting once. Remarkable.

thought: they have told nobody, and he would know
line: Good. You have told nobody. I would know if you had.

thought: aside: Hassan chose better than usual for once
line: The Chancellor chose better than usual, it seems.

thought: his daughter approves of them, and she approves of nobody
line: Quiet work so far. My daughter approves, and she approves of nobody.

thought: there's a spy's patience in them; he hopes it holds near Draynor
line: There is a spy's patience in you somewhere. Keep it till Draynor.

thought: they're dawdling while the prince is still held
line: Still here? The prince is not getting any less kidnapped.

thought: they walk so loudly Keli's men could hear them from afar
line: Walk like that and Keli's men will hear you from Lumbridge.

thought: his daughter is on watch while this one dawdles
line: My daughter is watching that jail while you dawdle about here.

thought: it's a key, not a siege; no war please
line: Do try not to start a war. It is a key, not a siege.

thought: so this is the city's hope; he keeps a straight face
line: So you are the hope of Al Kharid. How very... brave of us.

thought: if Keli catches them, he never met them
line: If Keli spots you first, I shall deny ever having met you.

thought: they rush about in daylight; spies work at night
line: Rushing about in broad daylight. Spies do this at night, you know.

thought: aside to a guard: off to save a prince, at a stroll
line: Look at that one, off to save a prince at a gentle stroll.

thought: the Emir rests and the paperwork doesn't
line: The Emir rests, and the ledgers do not. Neither, it seems, do I.

thought: someone has been climbing the palace window again
line: Someone has been climbing in at the palace window again. Disgraceful.

thought: his maxim: water first, then gold
line: Count the wells before the coins, I always say.

thought: the Arena's renovation shows in his accounts
line: The Emir's Arena cost us dearly. I have the accounts to prove it.

thought: he must consult Osman, who will tell him nothing
line: I must see Osman. He will tell me nothing, of course.

thought: quiet pride in founding the Spirit Anglers
line: The Spirit Anglers were my doing, more or less. I called the meeting.

thought: petitions about water pile up on his desk
line: Another petition about water. One cannot drink petitions.

thought: the palace warriors are for show and duty, not for challenging
line: Our warriors are here to guard the palace, not to be fought for sport.

thought: a visitor with manners; the city is glad of those
line: A visitor with manners. Al Kharid is always glad of those.

thought: they have the bearing of someone who gets things done
line: You have the bearing of someone who gets things done. We notice.

thought: measures them by the Emir's approval
line: The Emir would approve of you, I think. He is a fine judge of people.

thought: they bear the desert heat with dignity
line: Welcome to Al Kharid. You carry yourself well in this heat.

thought: they walked round the palace rather than up it
line: Ah, a traveller who walks round the palace, not up it. Thank you.

thought: aside to a palace servant: courteous and capable, a rare pair
line: Courteous and capable, by the look of it. A rare pairing in a visitor.

thought: the city is richer for guests like them
line: Our city is the richer for guests like yourself.

thought: they never once complained of the heat; noted
line: Not one complaint about the heat from you. I shall tell the Emir.

thought: they're eyeing the big window; doors exist
line: Do not even think of the window. We have doors, you know.

thought: visitors usually bow; a nod would do
line: Visitors usually bow. Or nod. A nod would do.

thought: yet another adventurer wanting to fight the palace warriors
line: One more adventurer asking to fight our warriors, and I shall retire.

thought: if they've come to complain of the heat, the gate is that way
line: If you have come to complain of the heat, the gate is that way.

thought: aside to a guard: watch that one near the windows, politely
line: Do watch that one near the windows. Discreetly, of course.

thought: they strike him as a person who climbs things
line: With respect, you strike me as a person who climbs things.

thought: the accounts balance, unlike their manners
line: The accounts balance, which is more than I can say for your manners.

thought: they're loitering somewhere unsuitable near the palace
line: Kindly stand somewhere a little less... adventurous.

thought: the palace tiptoes about since the prince was taken
line: Our prince taken, and the whole palace walking on eggshells.

thought: he needs someone reliable, not a show-off
line: I need someone who can get a job done. Not a hero. Someone reliable.

thought: Osman has methods Hassan prefers not to know
line: Osman has his methods. I have learnt not to ask what they are.

thought: how to tell the Emir there's still no news
line: How does one tell the Emir that his son is still not found?

thought: the accounts can wait, the prince can't
line: The accounts can wait. The prince cannot.

thought: every courtier has a theory, none a plan
line: Every courtier has a theory, and not one of them has a plan.

thought: the palace feels quiet without the prince
line: A palace without its prince is a very quiet place.

thought: Osman counsels patience but Hassan has to answer for it
line: Osman counsels patience. Osman does not have to run the palace.

thought: they look capable, which matters these days
line: You have a capable look about you. These days, that is worth noticing.

thought: aside to a guard: there goes someone who looks like they finish things
line: There goes someone who looks as though they finish what they begin.

thought: they seem the dependable sort, which the palace lacks
line: If I may say so, you seem the dependable sort. We could use one.

thought: someone with purpose in their stride; the city needs that now
line: Ah. Purpose in your stride. Al Kharid has need of that just now.

thought: the Emir values those who see things through
line: The Emir values people who see things through. You look one such.

thought: in dark days a steady face is welcome
line: Welcome, traveller. In darker days, a steady face is a comfort.

thought: they've travelled far and kept their head
line: Travelled far, I think, and kept your head. Admirable.

thought: he apologises for staring; he's always looking for capable people now
line: Forgive my staring. I am always looking for capable people these days.

thought: the palace needs someone capable; don't take it personally
line: The palace needs someone capable. Do not take that personally.

thought: he's looking for someone who can get a job done, still
line: I am looking for someone who can get a job done. I shall keep looking.

thought: prince missing, and they admire the architecture
line: Our prince is missing, and you are admiring the architecture?

thought: something tells him they'd ask about payment first
line: Something tells me you would ask about payment first.

thought: with the prince gone every offer counts, even theirs
line: With the prince gone we must hear every offer. Even, it seems, yours.

thought: no climbing while the palace is in mourning, well, worry
line: Kindly do not climb the palace while we are in mourning. Well, worry.

thought: aside: the prince taken and adventurers come to gawp
line: The prince is taken, and the adventurers come to gawp at the windows.

thought: he can usually tell whether someone is capable
line: Are you capable? Do not answer, one can usually tell.

thought: the reward is ready and he's counted it twice
line: The reward is counted and waiting. I counted it twice.

thought: Osman says a plan is in hand and nothing more
line: Osman tells me a plan is in hand. Osman tells me very little else.

thought: he's told the Emir there is hope; hopes it's true
line: I have told the Emir there is hope. I do hope I have not lied.

thought: the Emir asks after his son constantly
line: Every hour the prince is away, the Emir asks again.

thought: the prince's rooms are kept ready, optimism or habit
line: The prince's rooms are aired and ready. Optimism, or habit.

thought: the city can afford the reward but not the loss
line: We can afford the reward. We cannot afford to lose the prince.

thought: someone is finally acting; maybe he'll sleep
line: Someone is finally doing something. I may even sleep tonight.

thought: Osman's secrecy reaches even the Chancellor
line: Not even the Chancellor may know the plan, says Osman. My own palace!

thought: they're helping Osman; the palace is grateful already
line: You are the one helping Osman. The palace is in your debt already.

thought: thanks for taking it on; the Emir will hear
line: Thank you for taking this on. The Emir will hear of it.

thought: Osman trusts slowly; if he trusts them, so does Hassan
line: Osman does not trust easily. If he trusts you, so do I.

thought: the reward waits on the prince's return; confidence in them
line: Your reward is ready whenever the prince is. I have every confidence.

thought: it does an old official good to see real effort
line: It does an old chancellor good to see someone actually trying.

thought: aside to the court: there goes the one who answered for the prince
line: There goes the one who answered for the prince. Every courtesy, now.

thought: he takes some credit for spotting them
line: I knew you were the capable sort. I said as much to Osman, roughly.

thought: water for life if they bring him home
line: Bring him home and you shall never pay for water in this city again.

thought: polite reminder that the prince isn't home
line: The prince is still not home. I mention it only in passing.

thought: politeness as a weapon: don't let him keep them
line: Do not let me keep you. Truly. The prince is waiting.

thought: the reward is for bringing him back, not for visits
line: You are aware the reward is for bringing him back, not visiting me?

thought: Osman vouches for them; Osman has been wrong before
line: Osman assures me you are capable. Osman has been wrong before.

thought: they're strolling; he hopes the prince enjoys the wait
line: Strolling, I see. I do hope the prince is enjoying his wait.

thought: what to tell the Emir: that they were browsing?
line: The Emir asks after his son daily. Shall I tell him you were browsing?

thought: it's a reward, not a pension
line: We are paying a reward for this, you understand. Not a pension.

thought: he'd offer water but they'd stop to drink it
line: I would offer you water, but I fear you would stop to drink it.

thought: his robes and papyrus are what the desert lacks
line: Robes and papyrus! The desert never has enough of either.

thought: one man, one stall, a whole city to sell to
line: Two hands for the whole of Al Kharid. I need more hands.

thought: the gnomes scoff at his carpets
line: The gnomes say my carpets will never take off. My carpets disagree.

thought: proud of his son at the Grand Exchange
line: My boy Farid sells at the Grand Exchange now. Takes after his father.

thought: sell a carpet and lose his monopoly? never
line: Sell a carpet? And have every rug merchant fly for himself? Never.

thought: Pollnivneach his start, Al Kharid his customers
line: Pollnivneach gave me my start. Al Kharid gives me my customers.

thought: business is always good, with him
line: Business is good, my friend. With me, business is always good.

thought: he never buys, as a matter of principle
line: I never buy, my friend. Buying is how a merchant becomes poor.

thought: a passer-by with apparent taste
line: My friend, you have the look of someone with excellent taste.

thought: a discerning customer, he can always tell
line: Ah, a customer of discernment! One sees so few.

thought: a fine traveller deserves a fine robe, which he sells
line: Such a fine traveller deserves a fine robe, and I happen to sell them.

thought: a special price, said to almost nobody
line: For you, my friend, a special price. I say that to almost nobody.

thought: a sharp eye that could almost sell like him
line: With an eye like yours you could sell. Nearly as well as me, even.

thought: they look like a person of means
line: I can see you are a person of means, my friend. Means and taste.

thought: he never forgets a good customer, and has decided this is one
line: I never forget a good customer, my friend. I shall not forget you.

thought: aside to the camel by his stall: there walks a customer with taste
line: Now there walks a customer with taste. Mark my words.

thought: browsing never made anyone rich
line: Browsing again? Browsing never made anyone rich, my friend.

thought: a heavy purse that never opens at his stall
line: Such a heavy purse, my friend, and it never once opens at my stall.

thought: they'd make a terrible merchant, walking past bargains
line: You would make a terrible merchant. You walk past every bargain.

thought: he could sell them a bucket they don't need, two even
line: I could sell you a bucket you do not need. I could sell you two.

thought: every adventurer needs a tinderbox, surely
line: An adventurer with nothing to buy? Every adventurer needs a tinderbox.

thought: a raw chicken would improve their day
line: Forgive me, my friend, but a raw chicken would improve your day.

thought: ignoring him like a gnome would
line: Ignoring me like a gnome, my friend? Very well. I can wait.

thought: haggling by walking away; he invented that
line: Haggling by walking away, my friend? I invented that trick.

thought: the nephew should be here by now
line: My nephew should be here by now. Pollnivneach is not so very far.

thought: still no nephew; the stall opens at dawn
line: Still no nephew. And the stall opens at dawn, every dawn.

thought: a month's wages to fetch him; the cost stings
line: A month of the boy's wages, just to fetch him. A month!

thought: with the boy here he could sell twice as much
line: If the boy were here, I could sell twice as much. Twice!

thought: family is family but punctual family is better
line: Family is family, my friend, but punctual family is better.

thought: who minds the stall while he sells?
line: Who minds the stall while I sell? Not my nephew, apparently.

thought: a nephew-shaped gap behind the counter
line: There is a nephew-shaped gap behind my counter, my friend.

thought: no dragons for a shopkeeper, only a missing nephew
line: No dragons to slay at a stall. Only a nephew to wait for.

thought: good feet for a long road south
line: Good strong feet, my friend. Feet that could reach Pollnivneach.

thought: they look trustworthy, and he has a nephew problem
line: You look trustworthy, my friend, and I have a nephew problem.

thought: a capable face; he could use one
line: Ah, a capable face! I could use a capable face, my friend.

thought: they'd make a better assistant than the one who never came
line: You would make a fine assistant. Better than the one who never came.

thought: they're clearly the reliable sort; rarer than an honest camel
line: Such a reliable look about you, my friend. Rarer than an honest camel.

thought: for a friend, robes nearly half price
line: For a friend like you, the robes are nearly half price. Nearly.

thought: aside to a camel: there goes someone who'd get to Pollnivneach and back
line: Now there goes someone who would get to Pollnivneach and back.

thought: someone who turns up when expected, unlike his nephew
line: A traveller who arrives when expected! A rare jewel, my friend.

thought: too busy to buy, too busy to help
line: Too busy to buy and too busy to help. What are you for, my friend?

thought: nephew lost somewhere, customer lost at his stall
line: My nephew is lost somewhere, and you are lost in front of my stall.

thought: he'd hire them, but would have to watch them
line: I would hire you myself, my friend, but I would have to watch you.

thought: they dawdle almost as well as the nephew
line: You dawdle, my friend, almost as well as my nephew does.

thought: not buying? stand aside for the customers
line: Not buying? Then at least stand aside for the customers.

thought: everyone wants a bargain, nobody wants a job
line: Everyone wants a bargain and nobody wants a job. Is that not so?

thought: not 'no', just 'later'
line: Not interested? I shall put you down as 'later', my friend.

thought: empty hands he could fill for a fair price
line: Such empty hands. I could fill them for a very fair price.

thought: sold a beard and headdress early; good day
line: A beard and a headdress, sold before breakfast. A good day.

thought: any word from the south? no
line: Any word from Pollnivneach? No? Then the boy is still out there.

thought: he keeps spare false beards; one never knows
line: I keep a spare false beard for emergencies. One never knows.

thought: someone is fetching the boy; coins are coming
line: Someone is finally fetching the boy. I can almost hear the coins.

thought: the nephew will be greeted by a stranger in a fake beard
line: My nephew will be so pleased to meet a stranger in a false beard.

thought: when the boy arrives he'll rest; no, he'll sell more
line: When the boy arrives I shall take a day off... no, I shall sell more.

thought: a month's wages for one nephew: expensive family
line: A month of wages for one nephew. Expensive family, mine.

thought: the beard was a bargain; could have charged double
line: That beard was a bargain. I could have charged double, and did not.

thought: the beard he sold them suited them
line: That beard suited you, my friend. Very convincing.

thought: off to fetch his nephew: a true friend of the family
line: Off to Pollnivneach for me? A true friend of the family!

thought: only they would go; he'll remember, at a discount
line: Only you would go. I shall remember that, my friend, at a discount.

thought: such dedication they might make a salesman
line: Such dedication! You would make a salesman yet, my friend.

thought: first look at new stock when the boy is back
line: When the boy is back, you shall have the first look at my new stock.

thought: with them on it the nephew is as good as home
line: A traveller of your talents, finding my nephew? He is as good as home.

thought: they bargain badly but travel well
line: You bargain badly but you travel well. I respect the second.

thought: in his headdress they'll pass for a local, nearly
line: With my headdress on, they will take you for a local. Nearly.

thought: still here? the road runs south
line: Still here? Pollnivneach is south, my friend. Very south.

thought: nephew out there, adventurer in here looking at buckets
line: My nephew is out there, and you are in here, looking at buckets.

thought: did the beard fall off? no refunds
line: Did the beard fall off already? I do not do refunds.

thought: another disguise will cost more now
line: If you need another disguise, I am afraid the price has gone up.

thought: slower and more stubborn than a camel
line: Slower than a camel with a grudge, my friend, and twice as stubborn.

thought: promised a nephew, not a sightseer
line: I was promised a nephew, my friend, not a sightseer.

thought: the boy will have a real beard by the time they get there
line: The boy will have grown a real beard by the time you get there.

thought: lost the way? buy papyrus and draw a map
line: Lost the way? Buy some papyrus from me and draw yourself a map.

thought: the gate needs mending; sand in the hinges
line: The gate needs mending again. Sand gets into everything, even hinges.

thought: a small toll and still they look at him like a bandit
line: A small toll, and still they look at me as if I were a bandit.

thought: a dry traveller came back through, waterskin empty
line: Another empty waterskin back through the gate, and a very dry owner.

thought: the cell is empty; suspicious
line: The cell is empty today. I always find that suspicious.

thought: his guards call his prices reasonable; he pays them
line: My guards say my price is very reasonable. I do pay their wages.

thought: the chest: his men carry it to the bank
line: Things left in the chest go to the bank. My men carry them. Simple.

thought: other passes down at Unkah
line: There are passes down at Unkah too. Same sand, different gate.

thought: someone he jailed walks free again; Port Sarim, he supposes
line: Someone I jailed is walking about free again. Port Sarim, I suppose.

thought: he wagers they actually read the billboard
line: Ah, effendi! I would wager you actually read the billboard.

thought: a traveller who pays the toll without complaint
line: A traveller who pays the toll without complaint! My favourite kind.

thought: he reckons the sands will give this one back
line: Something tells me the sands will give you back, effendi.

thought: a familiar face; they keep the peace, he keeps the gate
line: Hello again, friend. You keep the peace, and I keep the gate.

thought: sensible people pack a knife and water; they look sensible
line: Sensible folk bring a knife and a full waterskin. You look sensible.

thought: they don't walk like an outlaw; outlaws slink
line: No outlaw walks the way you do, friend. Outlaws slink.

thought: he'd trust them with the bank chest, and he trusts nobody
line: I would trust you with the bank chest, effendi, and I trust nobody.

thought: aside to his guard: the sands won't get that one
line: There goes someone the sands will not get. Mark it.

thought: thinking of declaring themselves an outlaw? the cell has room
line: Thinking of calling yourself an outlaw? The cell has room.

thought: they'll come back thirsty and blame him
line: You will come back thirsty, effendi, and you will blame me.

thought: cacti have more sense, and they stand still
line: I have seen cacti with more sense, effendi, and they stand still.

thought: did they read the billboard? of course not
line: Did you read the billboard? No, of course not.

thought: haggling over a small toll wounds him
line: Haggling over a small toll? With me? I am wounded, effendi.

thought: misattribution: did he lock them up once?
line: Did I not lock you up once? No? My mistake, effendi.

thought: the sands have swallowed people with more sense
line: The sands have swallowed travellers with far more sense than you.

thought: a fond farewell with a cell kept warm
line: So long, effendi. I shall keep a cell warm for you.

thought: Irena watches the gate all day
line: Poor Irena. She watches the gate from dawn to dusk.

thought: the girl went south and the gate hasn't seen her since
line: That girl went south, and my gate has not seen her since.

thought: Irena asks every morning and he has nothing to tell
line: Irena asks me every morning. Every morning I have nothing to tell her.

thought: days now; the desert doesn't give people back easily
line: Days, now. The desert does not give people back after days.

thought: he wishes he'd checked her waterskin
line: I should have looked at her waterskin more closely. I should have.

thought: his men watch for the girl and see only sand
line: My men keep watch for the girl. They see only sand.

thought: worse than any sandstorm: a mother crying at the gate
line: Worse than any sandstorm, a mother crying by the gate.

thought: could outlaws be to blame? he hopes not
line: No word of Irena's girl. Outlaws would not dare... would they?

thought: a capable traveller; Irena would be glad of them
line: A capable traveller, effendi. Irena would be glad to meet you.

thought: they go into the sands prepared
line: You go into the sands prepared, friend. Not everyone does.

thought: kind eyes; Irena could use those now
line: You have kind eyes. Irena could do with kind eyes just now.

thought: a steady face after a sorrowful week
line: Good to see a steady face. This gate has seen enough sorrow lately.

thought: some walk out of the desert again; they look like one
line: Some people walk out of the desert again, effendi. You look like one.

thought: a traveller who stops to listen
line: A traveller who stops to listen. Irena has had too few of those.

thought: they pay the toll and heed the billboard
line: You pay your toll and you mind the billboard. Rare virtues, effendi.

thought: aside to a guard: there's someone a mother could trust
line: There goes someone a mother could trust. Not many come through here.

thought: don't get lost as well; one is enough
line: Mind you do not get lost as well, effendi. One is enough.

thought: did they read the billboard or just look at it?
line: Did you read the billboard, effendi, or just admire the lettering?

thought: another self-declared outlaw joker
line: Outlaw, are you? Every joker says so. The cell has heard it all.

thought: heroes come through daily; the desert keeps some
line: Heroes come through here every day. The desert keeps quite a few.

thought: aside: that one never glanced at the billboard
line: That one never even glanced at the billboard. Mark my words.

thought: he'd rather sell them a robe than a pass
line: I would sell you a pass, effendi, but I would rather sell you a robe.

thought: the sort to go in without a waterskin
line: You look the sort to go in without a waterskin. Prove me wrong.

thought: Irena needs a hero; let's hope one comes along
line: Irena needs a hero. Let us both hope one comes along soon.

thought: Irena smiled today; someone is looking
line: Irena smiled today, for the first time in days. Someone is looking.

thought: brave, going after the girl; foolish maybe
line: Brave, going after the girl. Foolish, maybe, but brave.

thought: he keeps a waterskin by the gate for Ana's return
line: I keep a full waterskin by the gate for Ana, for when she comes back.

thought: he asks every traveller from the south
line: Every traveller from the south, I ask about the girl. Nothing yet.

thought: Irena has stopped crying and watches the dunes
line: Irena has stopped crying. Now she just watches the dunes.

thought: his men watch for two now: the girl and her finder
line: My men watch for two people now. The girl, and whoever finds her.

thought: hope is no trade; he only sells waterskins
line: Hope is a hard thing to sell. Luckily, I only sell waterskins.

thought: a wide desert, a small girl, but someone looking
line: The desert is wide and one girl is small. Still, someone is looking.

thought: recognises them as the one searching for Ana
line: You are the one looking for Ana? Brave, effendi. Truly brave.

thought: Irena talks of nobody else now
line: Irena talks of nobody but you now, friend.

thought: an extra waterskin for the searcher, on the house
line: Take an extra waterskin, friend. On the house, this once.

thought: going after another's child; he respects it
line: A brave thing, going after another's child. I respect it.

thought: if anyone can bring her home, he'd bet on them
line: If anyone can bring that girl home, effendi, I would bet on you.

thought: they gave a mother hope
line: You gave a mother hope. That is worth more than any pass I sell.

thought: the desert doesn't frighten them; it frightens him
line: The desert does not frighten you. Good. It frightens me.

thought: his men won't keep the searcher waiting
line: My men will not keep you waiting at the gate, friend. Not today.

thought: back already, without the girl?
line: Back already, and without the girl? The desert is that way, effendi.

thought: Irena's hopes rest on them; walk faster
line: Irena's hopes rest on you. I would walk a little faster.

thought: brave yes, prepared we'll see
line: Brave, yes. Prepared? We shall see, effendi.

thought: if they need rescuing too, he's not going in
line: If you need rescuing as well, I am not going in after you.

thought: hope they search better than they shop
line: I do hope you search better than you shop, friend.

thought: don't come back without her; well, do come back
line: Do not come back without her. Well, do come back, but with her.

thought: try not to be the next one Irena waits for
line: So long, effendi. Try not to be the next one Irena waits for.

thought: aside: a rescuer standing about at the gate
line: A rescuer standing about at my gate. Irena would be thrilled.
